subject: Re: 🔵{Brand} & MobUpps
body:
Hi RECIPIENT_NAME,
Following up on my earlier email about recovering abandoned bookers for {Brand}. Fresh angle: as of January 2026, mobile apps now hold 61.45% of online accommodation booking share, so the abandon-and-rebook gap that Hopper and Airbnb re-engage into is where most of your volume lives. With travel and hospitality CPA averaging near $44.73, deep-linking abandoners back to live availability decides your real cost per validated booking. We hold out a control so recovered bookings read as incremental. Worth comparing against your current mix?
angle: fresh angle: mobile-first booking shift Jan 2026 (sourced) + travel CPA benchmark ~$44.73
register_notes: Stage 2 EN travel_and_booking retargeting: acknowledges second follow-up and references prior; fresh angle = timely development (mobile apps 61.45% of accommodation booking share, Jan 2026, GlobeNewswire) + market CPA benchmark (~$44.73 travel/hospitality, whitelabelagency 2026), both web-verified and in enrichment_sources, never attributed to MobUpps; reuses parent brands Hopper/Airbnb only, no new brands; MobUpps holdout/incrementality reference carries no figure; exactly 1 question mark; no sign-off; no X-not-Y.
